title: Vintage Posters & Graphic Design
description: Public-domain poster art — Art Nouveau, Belle Époque, and golden-age design.

items.title: Gismonda
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's "Gismonda" is a renowned lithographic poster created for the celebrated actress Sarah Bernhardt. It dramatically features Bernhardt in an opulent, Byzantine-inspired costume, characteristic of Mucha's Art Nouveau style.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, sarah bernhardt, lithograph, decorative, theatrical, portrait
items.credit_line: This file comes from Gallica Digital Library and is available under the digital ID btv1b53140689b/f1

items.title: Moulin Rouge: La Goulue
items.description_narrative: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec's iconic poster, "Moulin Rouge: La Goulue," vividly advertises the famous Parisian cabaret with its dynamic composition. It features the popular dancer La Goulue and her partner Valentin le Désossé, captured in Lautrec's distinctive, energetic style.
items.tags: poster, cabaret, Montmartre, Belle Époque, lithography, nightlife, entertainment, Parisian
items.credit_line: HwHWsv1o7adJ3A at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Divan Japonais
items.description_narrative: This iconic lithograph by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec advertises the Divan Japonais, a Montmartre café-cabaret. It vividly captures the Parisian nightlife of the Belle Époque, featuring the performer Jane Avril and the critic Édouard Dujardin in the audience, with Yvette Guilbert's distinctive gloves and silhouette hinting at her presence on stage.
items.tags: poster, lithograph, cabaret, parisian nightlife, belle époque, montmartre, advertising, post-impressionism

items.title: Aristide Bruant dans son cabaret
items.description_narrative: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec frequently depicted the vibrant world of Parisian nightlife, immortalizing performers like Aristide Bruant. This iconic poster captures Bruant's distinctive stage persona, serving as both an advertisement and a lasting image of Belle Époque entertainment.
items.tags: parisian nightlife, cabaret, poster art, aristide bruant, performer, post-impressionism, belle époque

items.title: Jane Avril
items.description_narrative: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec's poster immortalizes the French can-can dancer Jane Avril, a prominent figure of Parisian nightlife. Characterized by its bold lines and striking color contrasts, the artwork captures the energy and allure of fin-de-siècle entertainment.
items.tags: parisian nightlife, can-can dancer, art nouveau, poster art, Belle Époque, entertainment, bohemian, vibrant

items.title: Reine de Joie
items.description_narrative: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec masterfully captured the vibrant energy and often gritty realities of Parisian nightlife, from cabarets to brothels. This artwork, titled "Reine de Joie," exemplifies his keen observation of the city's entertainers and demimonde figures during the Belle Époque.
items.tags: parisian nightlife, belle époque, lithography, post-impressionism, art nouveau, cabaret, figures, french art

items.title: La Revue Blanche
items.description_narrative: This iconic poster by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec advertises the influential French literary and art journal "La Revue Blanche." It features Misia Natanson, a prominent figure in Parisian artistic and intellectual circles, elegantly poised against a stark background.
items.tags: poster, lithography, misia natanson, paris, belle époque, advertising, art journal, bohemian life

items.title: May Belfort
items.cultural_context: Belle Époque, Post-Impressionism, French, Art Nouveau
items.description_narrative: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec captured the Irish chanteuse May Belfort, known for her child-like persona and signature green dress, often accompanied by a black cat. This lithograph, a striking example of Art Nouveau poster art, advertised her performances in Parisian cabarets during the Belle Époque.
items.tags: portrait, lithography, poster art, belle époque, cabaret, art nouveau, parisian life, post-impressionism

items.title: Job
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's iconic "Job" poster features a captivating woman with luxuriant hair, elegantly framed by stylized floral motifs characteristic of Art Nouveau. Created as an advertisement for cigarette papers, this work exemplifies Mucha's mastery in blending fine art aesthetics with commercial graphic design.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, advertisement, bohemian, female figure, decorative, graphic design, fin de siècle

items.title: Bières de la Meuse
items.description_narrative: This iconic poster by Alphonse Mucha features an elegant female figure, adorned with flowing hair and elaborate decorative motifs, embodying the graceful aesthetic of the Art Nouveau movement. Created as an advertisement for Bières de la Meuse, it exemplifies Mucha's mastery in commercial art and design.
items.tags: art nouveau, advertising, lithograph, poster art, woman, decorative, elegant, commercial

items.title: F. Champenois Imprimeur-Éditeur
items.description_narrative: This vibrant lithographic poster features a graceful woman adorned with flowing hair and intricate floral motifs, embodying the distinctive Art Nouveau aesthetic. Designed as an advertisement, it promotes the Parisian printer and publisher F. Champenois, for whom Mucha created numerous works.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, advertising, woman, decorative, elegant, graphic design, fin de siècle

items.title: Zodiac
items.cultural_context: Art Nouveau, Fin de siècle, European
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's "Zodiac" exemplifies the Art Nouveau style with its elegant depiction of a woman adorned with intricate jewelry and flowing hair, set against a backdrop of the twelve astrological symbols. Originally conceived as a calendar design, this iconic work showcases Mucha's mastery of decorative design and his signature blend of beauty and symbolism.
items.tags: art nouveau, symbolism, calendar, woman, astrology, decorative arts, graphic design

items.title: Rêverie
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's 'Rêverie' is a striking lithograph from 1897, depicting a serene female figure enveloped in the artist's signature intricate Art Nouveau ornamentation. Originally created as an advertisement and decorative panel, it exemplifies the elegance and flowing lines characteristic of the era.
items.tags: art nouveau, symbolism, female figure, decorative art, lithograph, fin de siècle, contemplation, graphic design

items.title: The Seasons: Spring
items.description_narrative: This elegant work depicts a graceful female figure embodying the spirit of spring, adorned with flowing hair and floral motifs characteristic of Mucha's distinctive style. Her serene expression and the decorative elements around her evoke a sense of renewal and natural beauty.
items.tags: spring, woman, art nouveau, allegory, decorative, nature, illustration

items.title: The Seasons: Autumn
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's "Autumn" from his renowned "The Seasons" series features an elegant female figure, characteristic of the Art Nouveau style. She is typically surrounded by symbolic elements like grapes and falling leaves, evoking the abundance and transition of the harvest season.
items.tags: art nouveau, female figure, allegory, nature, autumn, decorative, fin de siècle

items.title: La Dame aux Camélias
items.description_narrative: Alphonse Mucha's iconic poster for Sarah Bernhardt's performance of *La Dame aux Camélias* showcases the celebrated actress in a lavish, decorative composition. This pivotal work, characterized by its flowing lines, Byzantine-inspired motifs, and ethereal female form, is a quintessential example of the Art Nouveau style.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, sarah bernhardt, theatre, decorative arts, lithograph, paris, female figure
items.credit_line: Original file from Library of Congress

items.title: Monaco Monte-Carlo
items.description_narrative: This lithographic poster by Alphonse Mucha captivates with its elegant female figure, emblematic of the Art Nouveau style. Created to promote Monaco Monte-Carlo, it showcases Mucha's distinctive decorative floral motifs and sinuous lines.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, lithograph, woman, decorative, elegant, monte carlo, advertising

items.title: Le Chat Noir
items.cultural_context: Art Nouveau, Fin de siècle Paris
items.description_narrative: Théophile Steinlen's iconic poster, "Le Chat Noir," advertises the famous Parisian cabaret of the same name. It features a striking black cat with piercing yellow eyes, often depicted with an aura or halo, against a stark background to attract attention.
items.tags: poster art, art nouveau, cabaret, parisian nightlife, cat, advertisement, fin de siècle

items.title: Folies Bergère
items.description_narrative: Jules Chéret's vibrant poster for the Folies Bergère captures the lively spirit of Belle Époque Parisian entertainment. Known for his innovative lithography, Chéret's work helped define the aesthetics of modern advertising.
items.tags: poster, advertising, Belle Époque, entertainment, Parisian, lithography, art nouveau

items.title: Folies-Bergère, La Loïe Fuller
items.description_narrative: This vivid poster by Jules Chéret promotes a performance by the innovative dancer Loïe Fuller at the Folies-Bergère. The dynamic composition and striking colors capture the energy of her pioneering theatrical lighting effects.
items.tags: poster, cabaret, dance, performance, art nouveau, belle époque, french, advertising

items.title: Bal du Moulin Rouge
items.description_narrative: This vibrant poster, created by Jules Chéret, serves as a dynamic advertisement for the famous Moulin Rouge dance hall. It masterfully captures the energetic and festive spirit of Parisian nightlife during the Belle Époque.
items.tags: poster, lithograph, belle époque, parisian nightlife, advertisement, french art, dance hall

items.title: Salon des Cent
items.cultural_context: Art Nouveau, Fin de siècle, French
items.description_narrative: This vibrant poster by Eugène Grasset advertises the Salon des Cent, a prominent Parisian art exhibition and publisher active in the late 19th century. It showcases the distinctive graphic style and decorative elements characteristic of the period's emerging Art Nouveau movement.
items.tags: poster, graphic design, art nouveau, fin de siècle, exhibition, french art, symbolism, decorative arts

items.title: Absinthe Robette
items.description_narrative: Privat Livemont's iconic "Absinthe Robette" poster showcases a graceful woman adorned in Art Nouveau elegance, embodying the Belle Époque's sophisticated aesthetic. The design, characterized by sinuous lines and decorative motifs, serves as a striking advertisement for the popular alcoholic beverage.
items.tags: art nouveau, poster, advertising, belle époque, woman, absinthe, decorative

items.title: Bitter Campari
items.description_narrative: This iconic poster advertises Bitter Campari with a vibrant, energetic figure balancing a bottle, capturing immediate attention. Its bold design and striking colors exemplify early 20th-century commercial art.
items.tags: advertising, poster art, graphic design, art nouveau, italian, commercial art, vibrant, bitter campari

items.title: Maurin Quina
items.description_narrative: Leonetto Cappiello's dynamic poster for Maurin Quina features a green devil figure with a red cloak, dramatically uncorking a bottle of the aperitif. This iconic advertisement exemplifies Cappiello's innovative use of bold imagery to capture attention and promote a product.
items.tags: advertising, poster art, art nouveau, graphic design, aperitif, devil, french

items.title: See America Welcome to Montana
items.description_narrative: This artwork, "See America Welcome to Montana," was created under the WPA Federal Art Project, a New Deal initiative aimed at promoting civic pride and tourism. It encouraged Americans to explore the nation's natural beauty and diverse landscapes during a challenging economic period.
items.tags: montana, tourism, wpa, poster art, american, new deal, travel, graphic design

items.title: I Want You for U.S. Army
items.description_narrative: James Montgomery Flagg's iconic "I Want You for U.S. Army" poster features Uncle Sam pointing directly at the viewer, an impactful call to enlist. Created in 1917, this powerful image became one of the most recognizable symbols of American military recruitment and patriotism.
items.tags: propaganda, recruitment, world war i, uncle sam, illustration, american, patriotism, poster art
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsc.03521.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Destroy This Mad Brute
items.description_narrative: Harry R. Hopps's "Destroy This Mad Brute" is a powerful World War I propaganda poster designed to incite American enlistment. It dramatically depicts a monstrous, helmeted gorilla labeled "Kaiserism" clutching a semi-nude woman, symbolizing the perceived threat to civilization and liberty.
items.tags: propaganda, world war i, anti-german, enlistment, political, allegory, war

items.title: When Hearts are Trumps
items.description_narrative: This artwork, titled 'When Hearts are Trumps,' was created by the American artist Will H. Bradley. Bradley was a prominent figure in graphic design during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
items.tags: art nouveau, graphic design, poster, illustration, american art, late 19th century

items.title: Harper's March
items.cultural_context: Late 19th-century American graphic design, Art Nouveau influences
items.description_narrative: Edward Penfield's "Harper's March" (1897) exemplifies his pioneering work in American poster design, created during his influential tenure as art director for Harper's Magazine. This prominent illustration showcases his distinctive use of flat colors and bold outlines, characteristic of late 19th-century graphic arts.
items.tags: illustration, poster art, graphic design, advertising, art nouveau, american art, magazine cover
